L1.evidence: Dutt XVIII — Daśaratha asks "the purpose of thy coming"; the arrival itself is narrated in sarga 17, not loaded

L2.en: He asked what the sage wanted.
L2.speaker: DASHARATHA
L2.speaker_rule: DASHARATHA's statement, not narrator fact. Attributed in every language.

L3.en: And before the sage answered — he gave his word.
L3.hi: और ऋषि के कुछ कहने से पहले ही — वचन दे दिया।
L3.evidence: CLM-0001 — the promise is Daśaratha's own speech

L4.evidence: CLM-0001 — the scope of his promise

L5.en: The sage had not said it yet.
L5.hi: ऋषि ने अभी कहा ही नहीं था।

screenplay.en: He asked what the sage wanted.
And before the sage answered — he gave his word.
The sage had not said it yet.

sound.design:
Room tone, lattice light, one lamp. Water in beat 7 — the only rich sound in the film, and
it should be generous, because the gesture is. **No score at all.** Film 1 is the only film
in the arc with no music, which makes the low string entering in film 2 feel like a change
in the weather.
sound.room_tone: continues across a continuous join; never reseated

hero_frame.why: A guest drawing breath, and a king who has already promised. The only poster in the set with no jeopardy visible in it.
hero_frame.use: poster, share card, and the frame a stranger sees first

continuity._what: What must not change between cuts.
standing_rules: The lamp stays where it is. Its flame moves; its position does not.
Daśaratha's ring is on the right hand in every hand detail, in every film.
The throne is occupied in films 1–2 and empty from film 3 onward. It is never re-occupied.
Viśvāmitra's staff is planted at his right through films 1–4. It moves once, in film 5.
The sage's cloth and seated posture do not change across four films — that stillness is the performance and a shifted fold breaks it.
Once the king steps down in film 3, he does not return to the dais in any later shot.

per_join.continuous: The frame is IDENTICAL across the join — same plate, same grade, same room tone. Not a similar frame: the same one.
per_join.hard: Location or time has changed. Room tone changes with it.

never: Do not foreshadow. No shadow crossing the king, no cut to an empty cradle, no minister
Do not make the sage mysterious. He is a guest being honoured.
Do not show Rāma. He is not in this film and is not thought of in it.
Do not have the king say "anything" as a flourish. He says it the way people do when they
Do not end on the king. End on the sage, not speaking.
